Grammar Focus

Careful sales language for options and pressure.

Hedging And Tone

B2-C1 · practical

Use careful phrases to reduce pressure and sound precise in a sales conversation.

might | would | could

"What if we used a short demo and a small pilot instead of a long sales call?"

Use What if to suggest an option without pressure.

Jump to transcript

"What might still stop the project?"

Use might to ask about possible risk carefully.

Jump to transcript

Options With If / Would

B2 · practical

Use if, would, and could to discuss possible outcomes and next steps.

if | would | could

"If the system feels heavy, people will return to spreadsheets after one week."

Use if to connect a possible problem to its result.

Jump to transcript

"For your situation, I would judge options by three criteria."

Use would to make a recommendation sound careful.

Jump to transcript

Say It Yourself

  • Ask one diagnostic question before you sell.
  • Suggest one low-risk next step with What if or could.
